question: Name two optional pavement-marking features explicitly labeled in Figure 3D-1 at the roundabout.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3D-1 explicitly labels "Optional white diagonal markings" (on the splitter/channelizing area at an exit) and an "Optional" yellow edge line around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway. The figure also marks the YIELD word pavement markings as "Optional," which is a third permitted feature shown. Options (permitted): - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1) and may be used to channelize traffic." - "Channelizing lines (see Section 3B.08) and chevron and diagonal markings (see Section 3B.25) may be used on the approaches to and within the circulatory roadway of multi-lane roundabouts to separate traffic lanes, discourage lane changing, and/or compensate for off-tracking of larger trucks and vehicles." - "YIELD (word) (see Figure 3D-1) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts." Guidance (recommended): - Where a white edge line is used for the circulatory roadway, it should be a solid line adjacent to the splitter island and a wide dotted line across the lane(s) entering the roundabout (see Figure 3D-1). Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows a callout labeled "Optional white diagonal markings" pointing to the white hatched area near the east exit, and a leader labeled "Optional" pointing to the yellow inner edge line of the circulatory roadway, with another "Optional" leader indicating the YIELD word markings and yield-line arrangement on the southern approach. Citations: - Figure 3D-1 (p.596) - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Section 3D.02 Option §5 (p.595) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.03 Guidance §2 (p.595) - Section 3D.01 Support §4 (p.595)
gold_answer: Optional diagonal markings in the splitter island and an optional wide dotted extension of the circulatory roadway edge line.
